quā^drĭ-rēmĭs , e (quā^trĭrēmis , Not. Tir. p. 177), adj. quattuor-remus,
I.having four banks of oars: “machina,” Paul. Nol. Carm. 21, 73 .— Hence, subst.: quā^drĭ-rēmis , is, f., a vessel having four banks of oars, a quadrireme (class.): “egreditur Centuripinā quadriremi e portu,” Cic. Verr. 2, 5, 33, § 86 ; 2, 5, 34, § 88: “quinque,” Caes. B. C. 3, 24 ; Liv. 24, 33; Plin. 7, 56, 57, § 207; Inscr. Orell. 2671; 3629.— As adj., Paul. Nol. Carm. 21, 73.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
